subject: Proposal: blended vs tiered thresholds for bulk hosted pricing

Subject: Pricing structure options for 10B token/month forecast

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at HighScale is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We pulled together a conservative monthly forecast and expect to land around 8–12B tokens/month in steady state, with spikes up to ~16B during new product launches.

Before we get too deep on legal, finance asked for two candidate commercial structures so they can model total cost of ownership: 1) a single blended committed rate (one per-token price for the committed volume) and 2) a progressive / threshold-based schedule where unit price decreases stepwise as you hit higher monthly bands.

Can you provide concrete examples (numbers) for both approaches, plus suggested minimum monthly commitment, true-up cadence, and any rollover/credit mechanics? Also highlight any product constraints (e.g., model family substitution, rate-limited bursts) that would affect billing.

I've attached our usage estimate. Would like a short pro-forma we can put in front of finance by EOD Friday.

Best,
Ellie
Director, Platform Engineering
HighScale AI

Team — forwarding HighScale's ask (attached). They want two concrete commercial examples and a short pro-forma they can take to finance by Friday. Key constraints: 8–12B steady state, spikes to ~16B. They want simplicity (finance likes single line items) but product/org prefers tiered because it protects margins and encourages adoption.

Can pricing provide:

- Minimum monthly commit recommendation and true-up cadence (monthly vs quarterly)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing structure options for 10B token/month forecast — need recs

Quick thoughts and numbers for proposal. I modeled two canonical options (numbers are illustrative but reflect current cost curves):

Option A — Blended committed rate (single line item)- Term: 12 months, minimum monthly commit: 6B tokens (monthly true-up)- Blended committed price (example for 10B month): $0.00036 / token -> monthly bill = $3,600,000- Rationale: simplifies finance, predictable unit price. We price blended to land above our blended margin floor (assuming infra + ops overhead) — Marcus confirms margin is ~30% at $0.00036/token for hosted inference on gen-style workloads.

Option B — Progressive thresholds (banded pricing)- Tier structure (monthly tokens):
  - 0–1B: $0.00080 / token
  - 1B–5B: $0.00048 / token
  - 5B–20B: $0.00030 / token
- Example for a 10B month: 1B*$0.00080 + 4B*$0.00048 + 5B*$0.00030 = $1,904,000
- Minimum monthly commit: 4B tokens (quarterly true-up available)
- Rationale: aligns price to marginal cost, preserves margin on initial volume, gives customer visibility and upside as they scale. Better for upsell economics.

Additional commercial mechanics we should propose for both options:
- True-up cadence: monthly for blended, quarterly for progressive (reduces admin noise for progressive)- Rollover: credits expire after 3 months (if we require committed credits)- Intro concession: 20% credit against first-month invoice (one-time) to offset onboarding spikes- Model substitution: we reserve right to route to compatible model variants (same family) if exact replica not available; substitution pricing remains within 10% of committed unit rate; callout in SOW

Recommendation: lead with progressive thresholds for long-term unit economics and capacity signaling; offer a one-line blended option if finance insists on a single charge.

—Lauren
Senior Pricing Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_rate_comparison.pdf (two-sheet summary)

I agree with Lauren's framing. A few seller-side tweaks to make the deck easier for finance:
- Offer a 3-month blended introductory price (slightly below Option A) to make the first renewal easier.
- Include an illustrative pro-forma that shows 3 scenarios (conservative 8B, target 10B, aggressive 14B) under each option so finance can see variance.
- Add a clause for capacity priority: committed customers get reserved burst capacity up to +30% of commit with a surcharge (we should price that separately).

Marcus — please confirm the margin note and whether we can support 20% intro credit for the first month without dipping below margin floor.

—Ben
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Ellie
